level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: AI Agents and MCP in Depth
audience: Engineers who build agents, tool integrations and MCP servers that run reliably and safely in production.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of design, read-the-code, trace-the-loop and failure-mode questions.
scenarios: Exposing a product to AI agents through an MCP server
Building a coding or research agent with tools
Debugging an agent that loops, stalls or picks the wrong tool
Securing an agent that reads untrusted content
Cutting the cost and latency of a multi-step agent
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Code in fenced blocks with the right language. Question mix: ~35% design judgment (workflow vs agent, tool design, which MCP primitive), ~35% read or debug code, a tool schema, an MCP message exchange or an agent trace, ~30% failure-mode, cost and security reasoning. Verifiers MUST type-check every TypeScript/TSX example with `sh {{root}}/.pipeline/ts/check.sh <file>` (TypeScript 7.0 strict, Node 24; set NORUN=1 for .tsx or code that needs network; installed: zod 4, react 19, react-native 0.88 types, next 16, vitest 5, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32, @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.3, jose 6). Run every Python example and compute every number with {{root}}/.pipeline/py313/bin/python (CPython 3.13 + PyYAML) or {{root}}/.pipeline/py/bin/python (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn). Check MCP behaviour against the current specification at modelcontextprotocol.io (version 2026-07-28 is current: stateless, no initialize handshake or session header; Sampling, Roots and the HTTP+SSE transport deprecated; confirm everything against the spec text and changelog) and type-check SDK code against @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32. Claude API facts: version 2026-10-21 removes temperature/top_p/top_k (400 if sent), prefill is unsupported from Claude 4.6 on, forced tool_choice returns 400 on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.x; current models are the Claude 5 family (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-fable-5-1); verify against platform.claude.com/docs. Phrase prices and limits conceptually unless dated from docs. Teach provider-neutral patterns first, with Claude and OpenAI specifics as examples. Sources: modelcontextprotocol.io, github.com/modelcontextprotocol, platform.claude.com, docs.claude.com, anthropic.com (engineering posts), developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com, ai.google.dev, owasp.org (LLM Top 10 2025, agentic security), opentelemetry.io (GenAI conventions), arxiv.org for primary papers (ReAct, Reflexion, Toolformer), rfc-editor.org and oauth.net for OAuth; no Medium or vendor-marketing blogs.

domains.name: Agent architecture
skills: Workflows vs agents: prompt chaining, routing, parallelisation, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimiser, and when a plain workflow wins
The agent loop: model call, tool calls, observations, stop conditions, iteration and token budgets
Planning and reasoning patterns: ReAct, plan-and-execute, reflection, and extended thinking budgets
Multi-agent systems: sub-agents for context isolation, hand-offs, shared state, and when one agent is better
Human-in-the-loop: approval gates, interrupts, resumable runs and durable execution

domains.name: Tool design and tool use
skills: Writing tools for agents: names, descriptions, input schemas, consolidating vs splitting tools, avoiding tool bloat
Tool-call mechanics across providers: parallel calls, tool_choice, strict schemas, returning errors as results
Designing tool outputs: concise, token-efficient, paginated, with actionable errors and stable identifiers
Side-effecting tools: idempotency keys, dry runs, confirmations and rollback
Code execution and computer use as tools: sandboxes, timeouts, resource limits

domains.name: Model Context Protocol
skills: MCP architecture: hosts, clients and servers; tools, resources and prompts; capabilities and versioning
Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP; the stateless 2026 spec model and what was deprecated
Building an MCP server with the TypeScript SDK: tool registration with Zod schemas, structured content, errors, progress and cancellation
Authorization for remote MCP servers: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, protected resource metadata, token audience and scopes
Operating MCP servers: discovery, versioning, rate limits, logging, and exposing a product safely to other people's agents

domains.name: Context engineering and memory
skills: Context windows as a budget: what to put in, ordering, prompt caching and cache-friendly layouts
Long-running agents: compaction, summarisation, scratchpads and note files
Retrieval for agents: agentic search vs vector RAG, just-in-time loading of files and data
Memory across sessions: what to store, retrieval, staleness and user control
Instructions and skills: system prompts, project instruction files, progressive disclosure of procedures

domains.name: Evaluation, observability and cost
skills: Evaluating agents: task success, trajectory checks, tool-call accuracy, LLM judges with rubrics and human calibration
Building an eval set from real traces and failures; regression gating in CI
Tracing agents with OpenTelemetry GenAI spans: model calls, tool executions, token and latency attributes
Cost and latency control: model routing, smaller models for sub-tasks, caching, batching and parallel tool calls
Debugging failure modes: loops, premature stops, wrong tool choice, hallucinated arguments, context rot

domains.name: Security and safety for agents
skills: Prompt injection, direct and indirect: why tool results and retrieved content are untrusted, and the lethal trifecta of private data, untrusted content and exfiltration
Least privilege for agents: scoped credentials, per-tool permissions, allow-lists and egress controls
Sandboxing and isolation for code execution and browsing agents
MCP-specific risks: tool poisoning, rug pulls, confused deputy, token passthrough and server impersonation
Guardrails and monitoring: input/output filters, human approval for high-impact actions, audit logs, incident response
